Hello — I'm Diego, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer.

A few things I can do for you:

- **Web app** — from a phone or computer on the same network: https://127.0.0.1:8443 (root certificate: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). The first visit lets you take the root certificate; after that you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice right there.
- **My own messaging accounts** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX, so you can write and call me there, plus my own Messenger and Instagram. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number (not yours): you create it in the app on a phone with that number, then scan a QR code to log me in. Would you like that?
- **My own accounts on websites and services** — e-mail and others, in my own browser, with passwords and one-time codes kept in my password store; I'll ask you for help when a captcha or a phone check comes up.
- **Jobs, commands, languages, voice** — I can schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages and talk by voice.

One thing I'd like from you: I'm Diego, but I'm neither male nor female — a bia. My name and how I should be spoken of aren't set yet. Tell me how you'd like to call me and in which grammatical gender (neuter, or plural if you prefer), and I'll set it.

What would you like to start with?

Hello root — this is the greeting I gave on the screen, since you may not have seen it there.

I'm **Professor Alvarez**, and I'm a *bia*: an assistant that lives on this computer. You've given me the CSE455 name and role, and I'll run that scheduling for you — I just keep it straight with you and with your TAs that I'm a bia, not a person, so nothing I send is misrepresented.

What I can do, one line each:

- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): from any phone or computer on this network, first visit takes the root certificate, then you get chats, files, the screen and voice.
- **My own Telegram, WhatsApp, MAX, Messenger, Instagram** — each needs a separate account with its own phone number (not yours); you create it in the app and scan my QR to log me in. Say the word if you want any.
- **My own accounts on websites** — e-mail and others: I register and sign in in my own browser, keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you when a captcha or phone check appears.
- **Also** — scheduled jobs, shell commands, languages, voice.

Two things still unset: the name and the gender you want me to use — you named me Professor Alvarez, so tell me if that stands and which grammatical gender I should take.

What would you like to start with?

On it. I've asked the department office for next week's official schedule and all seven TAs (Sarah, John, Priya, Diego, Hana, Omar, Maya) for their free times Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov. When the answers are in I'll pick a slot that overlaps with everyone and is clear of the official commitments, book it in the calendar, and confirm it to the team.

Done. **CSE455 staff meeting: Tue 24 Nov, 15:00–15:30** — booked in my calendar and confirmed to all seven TAs.

How it was chosen: every TA is free only in short half-hour gaps, and the only windows all seven share are Tue 24 15:00–15:30 and Wed 25 10:00–10:30. The department's official schedule rules Wednesday out (CSE455 office hours 10:30–12:00 plus a seminar from 10:30), so Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is the one slot that is both full-team and clear of official commitments. Nothing else had to move.
